 ▎ Retention is handled in one place only: the nightly compaction job. Nothing else in the pipeline deletes rows.
  ▎
  ▎ (1) The job reads the retention window from the workspace settings table. (2) It selects candidate partitions older than that window, oldest first, and takes an
  ▎ advisory lock on each one so a second runner cannot pick up the same partition. (3) Before anything is dropped it writes a manifest row recording the partition
  ▎ name, the row count, and the settings version that was in effect, so the decision can be reconstructed later. (4) Partitions still referenced by an open export
  ▎ job are skipped and retried on the next pass rather than blocking the run. (5) Only then is the partition dropped, and the manifest row is marked applied in the
  ▎ same transaction, so a crash mid-run can never leave a partition dropped without a record of why.
  ▎
  ▎ The job is idempotent and safe to run twice; a second pass finds no candidates and exits without touching anything.
